elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY,” making the cap mutual.

elements.element: The fee-based cap amount includes fees both paid and payable.
elements.evidence: The cap includes only amounts “ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO” and omits payable but unpaid fees.

elements.element: The fee-based cap amount is measured over the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The lookback runs from “THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION,” not from the claim generally; this may omit claims resolved or asserted without a filed cause of action.

elements.element: The cap is no less than USD 1,000,000 when 12 months' fees are lower.
elements.evidence: No USD 1,000,000 floor or greater-of formulation appears.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that neither party has liability to the other for “INDIRECT” damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that neither party has liability to the other for “CONSEQUENTIAL” damages.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that Section 9's limitation does not apply to either party's breach of confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: There is no carve-out for data protection obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: There is no carve-out for security obligations.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes liability arising under Section 8, but the supplied operative language does not establish that Section 8 contains indemnification obligations. The non-operative margin comment cannot supply that missing identification.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly disapplies the limitation for either party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly disapplies the limitation for either party's “willful misconduct,” which is substantively equivalent to wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: There is no fraud carve-out.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: There is no express carve-out for infringement of the other party's intellectual property.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages subject to the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no exclusion of Customer payment obligations from damages or from the cap.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly applies to “EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY.”

elements.element: The mutual cap is based on 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is based on the total amount paid by Corio under the agreement during the immediately preceding 12 months, and the per-transaction narrowing has been removed.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Although liability under Section 8 is excluded, the supplied operative text does not identify Section 8 as an indemnification provision. The margin comment's characterization is non-operative and insufficient to establish compliance.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that the Section 9 limitation does not apply to either party's breach of confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly carves out either party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly carves out either party's willful misconduct.

result.reason: The redline establishes a mutual rolling 12-month paid-amount cap and expressly carves out confidentiality, gross negligence, and willful misconduct. It does not reach the preferred position because it lacks payable fees, the USD 1,000,000 floor, several required carve-outs, and payment-obligation treatment. It also does not demonstrably complete the fallback because the operative text supplied does not establish that Section 8 is an indemnification provision; that fact appears only in the non-operative margin comment. The phrase “the limitation set forth in this Section 9” is also imprecise because Section 9 contains both a liability cap and a damages exclusion.
